blinding_guess.why: objectutils reads __slots__ and _fields_and_field_types defensively: it checks both attributes exist and skips any slot whose key is not in _fields_and_field_types, and test_typedefs.py covers an extra internal slot (_check_fields). The only oddity is objectutils.py:224 indexing _fields_and_field_types[name[1:]] even for a slot without a leading underscore, which generated ROS 2 message classes do not produce.

notes: All five packet elements are consumed; rosapi provides none of them, so declares and not_declared are empty. sensor_msgs/JointState is not named anywhere in the snapshot (grep for JointState over the whole snapshot returns nothing); rosapi introspects arbitrary message types whose names arrive at run time in service requests (e.g. MessageDetails.type -> objectutils.get_typedef_recursive, rosapi_node:290; TopicsAndRawTypes -> get_typedef_full_text, rosapi_node:211-213), so JointState could be processed at run time but has no port or reference. std_msgs/Header is named only in the test expectations of test_stringify_field_types.py (as the nested header of sensor_msgs/Image and CameraInfo), not in runtime code, so it is listed in references without a port. The two api elements are Python attributes of rosidl-generated message classes loaded at run time via rosbridge_library ros_loader.get_message_instance; they are not communication entities, so QoS, rate and definition_id are null for those ports. The builtin_interfaces/Time port's QoS is that of the ~/get_time service which carries it; the create_service call sets no qos_profile, and the recorded values are the rclpy documented default (qos_profile_services_default) cited from the API documentation, not fetched (only definition files may be fetched). Default service deadline is unspecified, so deadline_ms is null. perm_grants records the glob allow-list parameters that restrict which topics, services and params rosapi exposes; they are not SROS2 permissions. The builtin_interfaces release tag for jazzy was not listed (only raw definition files may be fetched); tags 2.0.2 and 2.0.3 and the jazzy branch all resolve and give the same normalised hash.
